title: FinVista
subtitle: A native lending app that turned a paper-heavy loan into an eleven-step journey a first-time borrower can finish on their own phone.

overview.headline: One lending app for six products, urban and rural, agent and DIY
overview.intro: FinVista is a consumer lending app for a large Indian NBFC (client anonymized under NDA), serving borrowers across 500+ cities. I led UX across six products, with the two-wheeler flow as the proving ground.
overview.tldr: Paper-heavy, agent-only loan → 11-step native Android journey. Six products on one 100+ component system. Processing runs ~60% faster, agent training dropped ~40%.

productLandscape.intro: Six products, one system. I used the highest-volume one as the proving ground.

products.name: Two-Wheeler Loan
products.desc: New and used bikes, scooters, electric, mopeds. This case study is about this flow.

products.name: Consumer Durable · Personal · Used Car · Tractor · Three-Wheeler
products.desc: Five more loan products on the same 100+ component system.

primaryUsers.label: Sales Centre Executives
primaryUsers.desc: They process loans over phone and app, juggle a dozen applications at once, and own the compliance. Speed is their whole job.

primaryUsers.label: Loan Customers
primaryUsers.desc: First-time and repeat borrowers, applying for a two-wheeler loan on their own phone. Often the first time they've done anything financial digitally.

problem.headline: One app, two personas, six products, and a device gap from flagship to entry-level 2G
problem.intro: The old flow was paper, agents, and fragments. I had to design one app that worked on the borrower's own phone, on the executive's too, held up on 2G, and stayed RBI-compliant end to end.
problem.coreChallenge: One scalable Android app, reusable components, holding up across every device and network in India, staying compliant.

dimensions.title: Multi-Persona Complexity
dimensions.desc: Customers apply solo, executives process for them. Different goals, different literacy, same screens.

dimensions.title: Information Overload
dimensions.desc: One application is 40+ fields. Fit them on a phone without drowning anyone. The IA does the heavy lifting.

dimensions.title: Device and Network Diversity
dimensions.desc: Flagship on 5G to entry-level Android on village 2G. The app has to hold up across the whole gap.

research.headline: What the best Indian lending apps already do, and what they miss
research.intro: I pulled apart the leading Indian lending apps, sat with stakeholders, ran a heuristic sweep. The pattern was clear.

competitive.name: Navi
competitive.notes: Clean UI, one-step-at-a-time flow, intuitive micro-interactions.

competitive.name: KreditBee
competitive.notes: Stepped onboarding, progress tracking, help always in reach.

research.keyInsight: Every competitor nails a single-product flow. None solve multi-product, multi-persona. That gap is the opportunity: one flexible system for 6 products and 2 personas.

approach.title: Material Foundation
approach.desc: Built on Material and card layouts. Android users already know it.

approach.title: Clean and Minimal
approach.desc: One hierarchy, uncluttered surface. Matters most for the borrower with the least digital literacy.

approach.title: Progress Always Visible
approach.desc: Users always know where they are and what is next.

insights.headline: Two personas, one journey
insights.intro: Two archetypes, both served without forcing either into the other's workflow.

personas.name: Rahul Sharma
personas.quote: Move fast, keep the customer calm, never miss a compliance step.

challenges.d: Many customers at once. Every extra tap costs him.

goals.d: A call picks up exactly where the app left off.

personas.name: Ankita Agarwal
personas.quote: Give me a loan I understand, from my phone, with no hidden charges.

challenges.d: Cautious about sharing financial data. Needs visible safeguards first.

goals.d: Clear rate, EMI, fees, total. No fine print surprises.

principles.d: One category of fields at a time. The load never spikes.
Visible security cues, transparent consent, a plain reason for every field.
Agents need speed, customers need guidance. Same system, adaptive UX.

flow.headline: The Two-Wheeler loan journey in 11 steps
flow.intro: One screen, one job, progress always visible. Onboarding on one end, disbursement on the other.
flow.diagramCaption: Two-Wheeler loan journey: 11-step application flow from welcome to disbursement

tasks.d: Name, DOB, gender, marital status, live photo capture
PAN card or Form 60 verification and validation
Residence type, landmark, and pin code
Employment type, company name, and landmark
Applicant income and total household income
Vehicle type, make, model, scheme selection
Add-ons: InstaCard, Credit Shield, extended warranty
UPI ID, bank account, and mandate setup
Document capture and live photo verification
Review all details and submit application

design.headline: From wireframes to production
design.intro: Low-fi to lock IA, mid-fi for visual direction, high-fi sharpened against real feedback.

wireframes.intro: I explored the hardest screens in grayscale, options side by side.

batches.caption: Loan application: long form vs accordion vs stepped wizard. The wizard won.
Applications dashboard: plain list vs status cards vs grouping by stage. Status cards won.
Progress: top bar vs vertical stepper vs progress ring. The stepper kept every stage visible.

explorations.intro: Flat vs 3D icons, input styles, layout density. Tested with stakeholders, iterated.

images.caption: Flat vs 3D icons across tenure, loan amount, and add-on screens

finalDesign.intro: 16 screens from login to disbursement. Every screen holds a single action.

screens.title: Login & Authentication
screens.desc: Mobile number + OTP, with an employee login fallback.

screens.title: Applications Dashboard
screens.desc: Search, sort, filter with status badges.

screens.title: Dealer & Portfolio

screens.title: Personal Details

screens.title: Employment Info

screens.title: Vehicle Selection

screens.title: Add-On Products

screens.title: Co-Applicant

keyDecisions.d: One screen, one job. It mattered most for agents processing 15-20 applications a day.
Top-level percentage and step-level indicator. Orientation without overwhelm.
Every step opens with plain-language help. Reduces anxiety for first-time borrowers.
For existing customers: pre-populated fields with checkmarks and one-tap confirm.

designSystem.headline: A 100+ component library, one visual language across six products
designSystem.intro: Built in Figma on auto-layout, variants, and tokens, so engineering handoff stayed clean.
designSystem.panelsIntro: Four families: tokens, form controls, navigation, and content containers.

panels.caption: Icons and illustrations: functional icons, multi-color variants
Button system: primary, secondary, tertiary with all states
Form controls: inputs, checkboxes, progress, toasts, file upload
Cards and sheets: lead cards, VAS cards, dialogs, bottom sheets

designSystem.systemImpact: New product journeys assembled from existing components in days, not weeks.

validation.headline: Five rounds, twenty participants, one journey people could finish alone
validation.intro: No formal lab. I shared Figma prototypes with real users across five rounds, watched, and refined.

rounds.d: PM, analysts, engineering on wireframes. Surfaced the IA problem: scrollable multi-action screens overwhelmed everyone. I pivoted to one screen, one action.
Six executives on mid-fi. Nobody could find the way back to edit a completed step. Added persistent edit icons + visible step-back.
Five first-time borrowers on high-fi. Progress tracker confused them. Added dual progress (percentage + step count). Vehicle icons were the most-praised piece.

validation.outcome: The design moved from a scrollable, multi-action layout to a focused, single-screen journey both agents and first-time borrowers could finish alone.

impact.headline: From paper to digital
wentWell: One screen, one action killed form fatigue for both agents and customers
Progressive disclosure made the 11-step journey "not feel long"
Dual progress kept everyone oriented without anxiety
The early design system let later product journeys assemble in days
differently: Bring sales executives in on round one. Their deepest insight only surfaced in round two
Test on low-end Android devices sooner. Performance gaps appeared late
Design error states from the start, not against edge cases at the end
